entry.title: Revisiting Recent Trends in Self-Improving Agents for Autoresearch

link.title: Revisiting Recent Trends in Self-Improving Agents for Autoresearch

entry.content:
Methods

Takeaways

These papers highlight two ways to improve research agents: refresh their context, or train the roles that decide what to investigate next.

What’s the Next Step?

I see evaluation time as a major constraint on self-improving research agents. A promising idea still needs to be tested, and those tests can dominate the research budget. In DuoDiscover’s vLLM study, one full evaluation takes about 85 minutes. This points to two directions.

Use fewer evaluations

How can we find a better solution with fewer calls to the evaluator? Training-free methods can use past results to select more informative experiments and avoid repeating failed attempts. With training, a research policy can learn which directions are worth pursuing. Both aim for sample-efficient search: reaching a stronger verified result within a fixed evaluation budget.

Memento 3 offers a training-free example. The agent turns interaction feedback into a revisable handbook of environment rules, then compiles those rules into an executable world model. It checks the model against past observations and uses it to plan future actions. The LLM stays frozen; the handbook and simulator improve as evidence accumulates. This illustrates an algorithmic route to fewer real interactions: use what the agent has learned to guide its next attempt.

Make evaluations cheaper

Can a cheap approximation tell us which candidates deserve a full evaluation? Smaller test suites, shorter runs or surrogate models could make it possible to explore more candidates with the same resources.

DuoDiscover offers an example: agents develop optimization targets together with cheap, tailored proxy evaluators. They search using these proxies, then confirm improvements with the full evaluator. Fidelity tests also check whether proxy rankings still agree with full evaluations as the search progresses.

Working on self-improving agents, I’m always interested in the models people choose and the tasks they test them on. Some familiar tasks, such as Erdős problems and packing benchmarks, already seem close to saturation. I’ve collected the models and tasks from these papers below as a reference for planning new experiments.

  • Models — model choices, agent setups and evaluation budgets.
  • Tasks — benchmarks, evaluation time, resources and recent progress.
entry.summary: LLM agents work on one problem, using evaluation feedback to search for the best solution within a fixed evaluation budget.

entry.title: Revisiting PPO for LLM Post-Training
entry.content:
This post reviews PPO and related policy-gradient methods for large language models.

Need a refresher on PPO? Start with the basics.

Review of Recent Work

Agent: SAO, LVRL, CoPE, EasyPPO, FlashREINFORCE.

LLM: TEMPO, AC2, Score Centering, Decoupled PPO¹, BPCO, EasyPPO, FlashREINFORCE.

Where the papers intervene

Work RL setting Component What changes Models & Tasks Critic / judge
SAO Agent Rollouts · GAE · updates One rollout per prompt, asynchronous collection, skip-observation GAE, strict token masking, and more frequent critic updates. Models: Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507; TIR-finetuned initialization for math.

Tasks: Math with Python; SWE-bench Verified with OpenHands.		 Separate value model initialized from the policy checkpoint.
FlashREINFORCE Both Rollouts · baseline Uses $R_i- ar R_{\mathrm{batch}}$, sequence admission and per-trajectory averaging. No learned critic or $L_V$. Models: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B; Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Qwen3-30B-A3B.

Tasks: Math and Python tool use; ALFWorld.		 No critic.
TEMPO LLM Value feedback Uses $V(y_{\mathrm{complete}})-V(s_t)$ on unlabeled questions, with periodic critic recalibration on labeled data. Models: Qwen3-8B/14B-Base; OLMO3-7B-Base, after PPO initialization.

Tasks: Math and general reasoning, with unlabeled adaptation sets and separate held-out sets.		 Learned critic; GPT-OSS-120B judges general-domain answers.
AC2 LLM Chunk values · advantages Uses $v_i- ar v$ and critic target $ ar v$. For critic-ready problems, unfinished chunks receive $v_i=V(s\cdot c_i)$. Models: Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507.

Tasks: FineProofs-RL → IMO-ProofBench.		 Actor and generative critic share weights; DeepSeek-V4-Flash grades proofs.
Score Centering LLM Actor gradient Centers the weighted score: $w\psi_ heta-c(s)$, where $w$ is the importance weight, $\psi_ heta= abla\log\pi_ heta$ and $c(s)=\mathbb E_{a\sim\mu}[w\psi_ heta]$. Addresses drift from training–inference mismatch. Models: Qwen3-0.6B-Instruct; Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base.

Tasks: Countdown and INTELLECT-2 math, under controlled sampler–trainer mismatch.		 No learned critic in the controlled comparison; group-centered REINFORCE.
Decoupled PPO LLM¹ Probability ratios Separates behavior correction $ u/\mu$ from clipping around $\pi_ heta/ u$, where $ u$ is a recent proximal policy. Models: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct in the AReaL example.

Tasks: GSM8K. This row describes a released configuration, not a separate paper experiment.		 Separate critic initialized from the same checkpoint.
EasyPPO Both Critic weighting · updates Uses $\omega_x\propto1/\max(\hat\sigma_x,\varepsilon)$, retains truncated samples for the critic, filters them for the actor, and uses smaller critic minibatches. Models: Qwen3.5-9B-Base for math/search; Qwen3.5-9B after SFT for coding.

Tasks: DAPO-Math-17K → AIME24; FrontierSmith → FrontierCS; Search-R1.		 Learned token-value critic. DeepSeek-V3.1 supplies coding SFT trajectories.
BPCO LLM Critic · GAE · clipping Bounds values to the reward range, uses $Y_t=R$, preserves raw advantages, and adapts $\lambda_\pi$ to length. Optional privileged critic inputs; Divergence PPO clipping. Models: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B; Qwen3-30B-A3B Base/non-Base; Qwen3-4B-Base for rubrics.

Tasks: Math: DeepScaleR or DAPO-Math-17K → AIME25; OpenRubrics.		 Learned critic; optional answer/rubric inputs. Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 is the rubric judge.
LVRL Agent Value estimates · step credit A frozen LLM uses trajectory and group context to estimate values. Anchored value differences give action-level advantages; no critic optimization. Models: Qwen3-4B/8B for AppWorld and BabyAI; Qwen3-8B/32B for repository tasks.

Tasks: AppWorld, BabyAI; R2E-Gym → SWE-bench Verified.		 Frozen Claude Opus 4.6 value critic. LVOPD uses Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking-2507-FP8 as teacher and critic.
CoPE Agent Auxiliary policy loss Adds successful-trajectory action forecasting to GRPO on a shared backbone. It changes supervision, without adding a value critic. Models: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct; Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct for AppWorld.

Tasks: ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, τ²-bench and AppWorld.		 No value critic; acting and forecasting share one backbone.

¹ Decoupled PPO refers to the linked GSM8K example. AC2’s chunks divide a proof into segments, without external interaction.

See details on the tasks →

Key mechanisms

SAO

  • Single-rollout sampling: Collect one trajectory per prompt asynchronously. A learned critic supplies the baseline, so training need not wait for sibling rollouts.
  • Token masking: Compare current token probabilities with logged rollout probabilities. Mask tokens whose ratio falls outside the allowed interval, regardless of advantage sign.
  • Skip-observation GAE: Connect consecutive model actions across tool feedback, without computing GAE through observation tokens. The feedback remains in the next action’s context.
  • Critic updates: Warm up the critic, freeze its attention layers, and update it twice per actor update to help it track the changing policy.

FlashREINFORCE

  • No learned critic: Sample once per prompt and subtract the batch mean reward, across different prompts, to obtain signed advantages.

  • Trajectory filtering: Weight token updates by current-to-rollout probability ratios. For each sampled token, let $p_t$ and $q_t$ be its rollout and current-policy probabilities at the same history:

    \[ egin{aligned} d_t &= p_t\log rac{p_t}{q_t}+(1-p_t)\log rac{1-p_t}{1-q_t},\ ar D &= rac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^{T}d_t,\qquad m=\mathbf{1}[ ar D\leq\delta]. \end{aligned}\]

    Keep the whole trajectory only when $m=1$; $T$ counts model-generated tokens and $\delta$ is the threshold. This Bernoulli KL is a lower-bound proxy for full-vocabulary KL. Details.

  • Equal trajectory weight: Average over tokens within each trajectory, then over the batch. Long failures do not get extra weight simply for being long; each fresh batch receives one update.

TEMPO

  • Critic feedback at test time: On unlabeled questions, use the critic’s final-response score as reward and subtract its prefix predictions for token-level advantages.
  • Periodic recalibration: Retrain the critic on labeled questions with verified rewards, then resume policy adaptation. This keeps feedback tied to external supervision as the actor changes.

AC2

  • Short continuations: Sample prefixes from a replay buffer and generate several continuations. Once the critic passes readiness checks, stop at a chunk boundary and estimate the unfinished response’s value.
  • Chunk advantages: Subtract the group mean endpoint value from each continuation’s value. Train the shared generative critic to predict that group mean at the starting prefix.
  • Full-rollout audits: Still complete a fraction of ready problems to check critic accuracy against actual outcomes.

Score Centering

  • Center the gradient: “Score” means the log-probability gradient. Subtract its expected value under the sampler at each prefix to remove drift caused by sampler–trainer mismatch.
  • Practical correction: Store the sampler’s top-token probabilities and approximate the remaining probability mass. The correction can also be combined with importance weighting.

Decoupled PPO

  • Two probability ratios: Use proximal-policy / behavior-policy probabilities for sampling correction, and current-policy / proximal-policy probabilities for PPO clipping.
  • A recent clipping reference: The proximal policy is one training step behind the current policy. This separates the size of a new update from how stale its rollout is.

EasyPPO

  • Actor-only truncation filtering: Exclude overlong responses from actor updates but retain them for critic training, so value estimates include the risk of failing to finish.
  • Noise-weighted critic loss: Weight each prompt’s critic loss by the inverse standard deviation of its sampled returns. Prompts with more variable rewards have less influence.
  • Smaller critic minibatches: Apply gradient clipping to moderately smaller batches, limiting how many other samples an outlier can suppress. The actor retains the PPO objective.

BPCO

  • Ground the critic: Bound predictions to the reward range and regress directly on observed final rewards. Optional reference answers or rubrics go to the critic only.
  • Preserve the learning signal: Keep raw advantages and adapt GAE’s decay to response length, avoiding batch normalization that can amplify small residual signals.
  • Divergence PPO: Make clipping depend on the sampled token’s probability, rather than applying the same ratio bounds everywhere. This differs from Decoupled PPO above.

LVRL

  • Frozen LLM critic: Read completed trajectories and related rollouts to estimate intermediate values in hindsight; no critic training is needed.
  • Anchored credit: Fix the starting value to the group mean reward and the final value to the observed reward. Adjacent value differences assign credit to actions and sum to the outcome’s improvement over the group mean, before normalization.

CoPE

  • Forecast successful actions: Add a supervised loss that predicts several subsequent actions from a history in a successful rollout.
  • Shared policy backbone: Train acting with GRPO and forecasting with the auxiliary loss. At inference the model still acts one step at a time; the extra supervision does not require a value critic.
entry.summary: PPO and related policy-gradient methods for LLM post-training.
